subject: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates

messages.author: d4aac47c58d1e583
messages.subject: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates
parts:
My experience in R is very limited and I am currently trying to develop SECR density models for wild turkeys on 3 wildlife management areas. Specifically I would like to use multiple habitat covariates( in the form of rasters), such as distance to nearest road and distance to nearest food plot, in a single model.
I am assuming this is possible from the reading I have done so far.
Does anyone have example code for adding multiple covariates they would be willing to share?
Hopefully my questions are clear.  Any help or suggestions would be appreciated

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates
parts:
Welcome to the group!
The brushtail possum example in secr-densitysurfaces.pdf shows how you can use the addCovariates() function to transfer covariates from a spatial data source to the habitat mask used in 'secr'. The source there is a polygon coverage, but you can also use rasters. You might also check secr-spatialdata.pdf. Once you have covariates in the habitat mask they can be named in the density model e.g. D~forestcover. Don't expect too much - - it works best with few covariates.
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: SECR code for adding multiple mask covariates
parts: No further thoughts, or at least none I can back up with evidence. My sense is that SECR datasets often contain little information about spatial pattern in activity centres (AC), perhaps because there is uncertainty regarding the true location of each AC. In consequence, stratum-specific estimates of density tend to have wide CI. Your mileage may vary.
